subject.title: Feature Request: Stream Repetition Safeguard (Halt & Confirm)

question: What should OpenClaw do when assistant text or thinking output becomes semantically repetitive during an active stream?
rationale: The missing code path is clear, but default abort behavior, false-positive tolerance, confirmation/resume semantics, and session-history cleanup are product and compatibility decisions that automation should not invent.

options.title: Add guarded abort with cleanup
options.body: Implement a core repeated-text detector that aborts the active stream, suppresses buffered repetitive output, records a recoverable terminal state, and asks the user to cancel, retry, or reset rather than blindly resume the same stream.

options.title: Detector only, no confirmation
options.body: Add a lower-friction guard that aborts and reports the turn without a manual resume flow, reducing product surface but leaving recovery policy simpler.

options.title: Defer to timeout work
options.body: Leave semantic repetition unimplemented for now and rely on generation timeout work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8724, accepting that repeated active streams may continue until a timeout or token cap.

recommendation.title: Add guarded abort with cleanup
recommendation.body: Implement a core repeated-text detector that aborts the active stream, suppresses buffered repetitive output, records a recoverable terminal state, and asks the user to cancel, retry, or reset rather than blindly resume the same stream.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from stream-handler blame and the existing maintainer review context for this issue.
